name: Dot Matrix
tagline: Big numbers lit on a dot board that re-lights column by column, with hard cream-to-black cuts.
description: Hardware dot-board look: everything is spelled or drawn in round dots on a fixed grid, re-lit column by column behind a hot-pink scan line while the background cuts between cream and black, with mono HUD corners and a timecode. The preview is a stat reel of big numbers for a status page.

display.family: Dot grid (5×7 bitmap built from divs)
display.usage: 34px dots on a 44px pitch, 7 characters wide

body.usage: Uppercase captions 30px and HUD labels 18px, tracking 0.12–0.14em, in accent pink

transitions: hard background cut (cream ↔ black) on the scan line
board shifts half a character to keep odd-width content centred
textAnimations: lit dots pop in with a seeded pseudo-random stagger (never Math.random)
whole board breathes +12% from the centre once per stat
caption swaps and rises 16px after each relight

rhythm.notes: One number per beat of ~2.4s. The relight itself takes ~0.6s; let each number sit for at least 1.5s before the next sweep.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- Everything is drawn on a fixed board of round dots (e.g. 41×7 or larger), like hardware: unlit dots stay visible at 8% opacity and scale 0.55; lit dots are ink on cream #f1ede4 or hot pink #ff2e88 on black.
- Words and numbers use a 5×7 bitmap font on that grid; simple shapes or icons of the subject are drawn as dot bitmaps too. Never swap in a text font for the hero element.
- Change what the board shows by re-colouring dots column by column (~14.5ms per column) behind a hot-pink scan line, and cut the background between cream and black on the same frame.
- Lit dots pop in with a seeded pseudo-random stagger (index math, never Math.random) so parallel render workers agree; the board breathes +12% from the centre once per beat.
- Every big element gets a small uppercase JetBrains Mono caption saying exactly what it is, rising 16px after each relight.
- Frame with thin pink corner ticks, a section label top-left, a name top-right and a frame timecode bottom-left.
- Avoid gradients, soft glows, photos and smooth morphs; changes are hard and clicky.
example: The preview is a status-page stat reel: big numbers lit on a 41×7 dot board that re-lights column by column with captions like incidents caught. Don't copy this scene unless asked.
